annotation.title_clean: Artificial Intelligence and Media and Information Literacy in Africa: A Framework for Trust, Critical Evaluation, and Ethical Engagement, Kenya
annotation.title_en: Artificial Intelligence and Media and Information Literacy in Africa: A Framework for Trust, Critical Evaluation, and Ethical Engagement, Kenya
annotation.venue: Journal of the Kenya National Commission for UNESCO
annotation.summary_en: Journal article page presenting a PRISMA-based review of 68 sources and proposing an AI-Integrated Media and Information Literacy framework for Africa, with five components: algorithmic awareness, critical evaluation, trust calibration, ethical engagement and digital inclusion. It concerns AI-mediated information, not robots.
key_provisions_or_claims: Traditional MIL frameworks are insufficient for AI-mediated communication.
Proposes the AI-MIL framework with five interdependent components.
Reframes literacy as calibrated trust rather than blanket scepticism.
Centres African realities: mobile-first access, encrypted-network misinformation, linguistic diversity.
Yields five testable propositions for future empirical research.
